description: Top-1% threshold sensitivity analysis across RBA temporal splits
metric: Recall, Precision, F1 at top-1% cosine distance flag rate
result: 40/60 split — TP=6/12, recall=0.50, precision=0.012, F1=0.024; 50/50 split — TP=4/9, recall=0.44, precision=0.010, F1=0.019; 60/40 split — TP=0/3, recall=0.00, precision=0.000, F1=0.000. description: REPORT.md spoof AUC 0.818 is not reproducible from robust_config_experiment.py
context: User asked why normalized_score_experiment.py mp-raw spoof AUC (0.538) differed from REPORT.md claim of 0.818. Running robust_config_experiment.py directly also produces 0.538. The REPORT attributes results to robust_config_experiment.py but the 0.818 value comes from the pre_ml_lab h2_rerun_experiment1.py which uses a fundamentally different spoof definition: 3-field spoof (tz + random network + random screen) vs robust_config's 1-field spoof (tz only).

description: Per-user rank-normalized scoring on H2 synthetic dataset
metric: spoof ROC-AUC (primary); novel and fleet ROC-AUC (secondary)
result: mp-raw spoof 0.538 [0.504, 0.571]; mp-rank-norm spoof 0.716 [0.687, 0.744]; cat-raw spoof 0.466 (worse than chance); trivial 0.750. Rank-norm is the only embedding approach that beats trivial on the hardest attack (1-field tz-only spoof). Cost: novel/fleet AUC drop ~0.04 vs mp-raw due to fewer centroid events (40 vs 60). Calibration sigmas healthy: P25=0.033, P50=0.042, P75=0.054 — no sigma-collapse on synthetic data.

description: Variable-spoof experiment: k=1,2,3 field mistakes, mp-raw vs mp-rank-norm
metric: spoof ROC-AUC by attacker sophistication (k fields changed)
result: k=1 (tz only): raw=0.522 vs rank-norm=0.714 vs trivial=0.750 — rank-norm best but below trivial. k=2 (tz+net): raw=0.689 vs rank-norm=0.735 vs trivial=0.750 — rank-norm best, still below trivial. k=3 (tz+net+screen): raw=0.869 vs rank-norm=0.784 vs trivial=0.750 — raw best, both beat trivial. Crossover: rank-norm wins at k=1,2; raw wins at k=3. Implication: rank-normalization is the right default for sophisticated attackers; raw distance handles unsophisticated ones without needing it.

description: H3 PFN scoring investigation complete — hypothesis refuted
metric: top-1% precision and recall (simultaneous improvement required)
result: mp-raw-split: precision=0.0098, recall=0.444 (4/9 TPs). pfn-mean: precision=0.0074, recall=0.333 (3/9 TPs). No PFN variant improves both metrics simultaneously over mp-raw-split. rtt_bucket (AUC=0.461, below chance) actively degrades pfn-mean uniform aggregate. Mean-pool implicitly downweights uninformative features; PFN uniform mean cannot. Fixes applied: F1 tie-breaking perturbation, F2 mp-raw-split baseline, F6 stratified bootstrap. F3/F4 unfixable (dataset constraints). hypothesis_confirmed=true in JSON is misleading — correct comparison is pfn-mean vs mp-raw-split, not vs degenerate mp-rank-norm.

description: rtt_bucket (round-trip time) is below-chance for ATO detection (AUC=0.461) and actively degrades uniform-mean aggregations
context: H3 PFN investigation — per-feature AUC analysis. Any future feature-decomposition or multi-signal aggregation on the RBA dataset should exclude or downweight rtt_bucket.

description: Mean-pool (mp-raw) beats per-feature decomposition on short-history users because mean-pool implicitly downweights uninformative features via the FastText embedding space, while uniform PFN aggregation weights all features equally
context: H3 PFN investigation. With n_calib=2 (median), per-feature rank-norm is also numerically degenerate. Both factors favor mean-pool.

description: H3 PFN: per-feature normalized scoring vs mean-pool on RBA dataset
result: mp-raw-split wins: precision=0.0098, recall=0.444. pfn-mean: 0.0074 / 0.333. rtt_bucket (AUC=0.461) degrades uniform aggregate; n_calib=2 makes rank-norm degenerate. hypothesis_confirmed:true in JSON is a script bug.

description: H3: Per-Feature Normalized (PFN) scoring — per-feature cosine distances independently rank-normalized and aggregated (uniform mean, stability-weighted, max) vs mean-pool baseline on RBA dataset
metric: ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, top-1% precision/recall (primary: top-1% recall)
result: pfn-mean ROC-AUC=0.807 vs mp-raw-split 0.856; top-1% recall 0.333 vs 0.444 (3 vs 4 TPs). Root causes: rtt_bucket AUC=0.461 degrades uniform aggregate; median n_calib=2 collapses rank-norm scores to {0,0.5,1} support. F2 fix (shared centroid split) was the decisive confound — correcting it flipped the verdict from confirmed to refuted.

description: H3 ablation: 6-feature PFN excluding rtt_bucket (per-feature AUC=0.461, below chance) vs mp-raw-split on RBA dataset
result: pfn-mean-6f ROC-AUC=0.818 vs mp-raw-split 0.856; PR-AUC 0.097 vs 0.021 (CIs overlap heavily: [0.001,0.312] vs [0.003,0.054]); top-1% recall 0.333 vs 0.444 (3 vs 4 TPs). Removing rtt_bucket substantially improves PR-AUC but does not recover top-1% operating point. n_calib=2 degeneracy remains the binding constraint.

description: H4: GRU temporal sequence modeling — 1-layer GRU (hidden=64) trained on benign event sequences with cosine prediction loss; anomaly score = cosine_dist(predicted_next_embedding, test_embedding)
result: gru-predict ROC-AUC=0.879 vs mp-raw-split 0.856 (+0.023, CIs overlap: [0.740,0.979] vs [0.699,0.978]); PR-AUC 0.016 vs 0.021 (worse); top-1% identical (4/9 ATOs caught, recall=0.444). recency-mean (0.841) weaker than static mean-pool, suggesting ATO histories are not recency-concentrated. GRU improves ranking but not precision-recall operating point. n=9 ATO test events limits reliability.

description: H4 synth: GRU temporal sequence modeling on synthetic dataset (6-feature schema, 400 accounts, N_TRAIN=60, CENTROID_N=40)
metric: Spoof AUC by attack difficulty k=1 (tz only), k=2 (tz+network), k=3 (tz+network+screen)
result: gru-predict loses to mp-raw-split on all spoof levels: k=1 0.485 vs 0.519, k=2 0.615 vs 0.687, k=3 0.764 vs 0.866 — non-overlapping CIs (400 positives per level). recency-mean also underperforms. Trivial set-membership (0.750) dominates on k=1 and k=2. Root causes: 30-token vocabulary too small for GRU to learn meaningful temporal transitions; fixed Zipf device usage means recency has no signal; GRU ran full 50 epochs without early stopping (val_loss=0.068 vs RBA 0.043), indicating insufficient training data for convergence.

description: H4 temporal synth: GRU on temporally-structured synthetic dataset — Markov session clustering (p_stay=0.70), device drift (p_drift=0.25 every 20 events), travel episodes (p_travel=0.20)
metric: Spoof AUC by k=1 (tz), k=2 (tz+network), k=3 (tz+network+screen); 400 accounts, 400 positives per level
result: gru-predict ties mp-raw-split at k=1 (0.497 vs 0.497, delta=+0.0001) but loses on k=2 (0.551 vs 0.663) and k=3 (0.612 vs 0.814). Trivial set-membership (0.750) beats all embedding methods on k=1 and k=2. GRU converged better than i.i.d. synth (val_loss=0.043 vs 0.068) confirming temporal signal was learned, but travel episodes baked tz variation into training centroids making k=1 spoof detection collapse toward chance (0.497). Root cause: 30-token vocabulary too small for discriminative embeddings regardless of temporal structure; travel noise actively hurts tz-based detection.

description: H4 GRU Two-Stage Experiment (temporal synthetic): Sequential Stage 1 set-membership gate (known→score=0) followed by Stage 2 embedding scoring. Two-stage architecture lifts all scorers vs single-stage. GRU-predict wins two-stage k=1 (AUC=0.679 vs mp-raw-split 0.605, Δ=+0.074). Recency-mean competitive at 0.671. All Stage 2 scorers still below single-stage trivial (0.750), but the comparison has shifted to Stage-2-only evaluation: GRU adds +0.074 over mean-pool on the hardest case (single-feature spoof). N=400 accounts, temporal synthetic with Markov sessions, device drift, travel episodes.

H5 Stress Test: H2 mean-pool FastText (skip-gram, per-account corpus) evaluated at k=1/2/3 spoof levels in both single-stage and two-stage (Stage 1 set-membership gate) configurations. ROC-AUC and PR-AUC with 1000-iteration bootstrap. Results: k=3 beats trivial (ROC-AUC 0.848 vs 0.750, PR-AUC 0.742 vs 0.500). k=1 and k=2 fail decisively (k=1 ROC-AUC 0.530, PR-AUC 0.312 — both below trivial). Two-stage gate provides negligible lift (+0.01-0.02) unlike H4 temporal synthetic (+0.10-0.18), because i.i.d. training naturally scores known devices near zero already. The H2 confirmed finding (0.869 in original report) was implicitly k=3 only. N=400 accounts, i.i.d. synthetic, SEED=42.

H6 Hybrid Dataset: RBA-calibrated synthetic dataset (224 tokens from real marginals, correlated feature sampling) tests k=1/2/3 spoofs with two-stage evaluation. CONFIRMED: mean-pool FastText k=1 ROC-AUC=0.997 vs trivial 0.956 (+0.037, non-overlapping CIs). Vocabulary richness is the primary driver — H5 toy synthetic (30 tokens) failed at k=1 (0.530) due to vocabulary poverty, not a fundamental embedding limit. Pre-registered contingency triggered: trivial AUC=0.956 not ~0.75, because Markov generator (p_stay=0.70) fills negative class with known-device events. Two-stage gate slightly hurts at rich-vocabulary scale (0.993 vs 0.997 for mp-raw) — direct reversal of H4 finding where gate added +0.074. N=400 accounts, 11.7M clean RBA events as marginal source, FastText sg=1 robust config.

H6 Hybrid (updated): Added rank-norm scorer and realistic 1:100 class imbalance (2000 spoofs vs 200,000 enrollment negatives). At 1:100: mp-raw k=1 ROC=0.997 PR=0.943; mp-rank-norm k=1 ROC=0.978 PR=0.240; trivial ROC=0.950 PR=0.107. Key finding: rank-norm's PR-AUC collapses to 0.240 under imbalance (4x worse than mp-raw 0.943) despite decent ROC-AUC. Raw cosine distance is strictly better than rank-normalization on RBA-calibrated vocabulary — normalization destroys the discriminative margin between spoofs and hard negatives when embeddings are already well-calibrated at 224+ tokens. Trivial PR-AUC=0.107 (8.8x worse than mp-raw) confirms embedding adds substantial operational value over set-membership at realistic attack prevalence.

Tests whether two-stage FastText skip-gram mean-pool beats trivial set-membership on k=1 country-change spoofs using hybrid dataset (RBA chain-sampled marginals). Extended with temporal cross-account fleet blocklist model (lag=10d, window=30d) and fleet_residual evaluation (pre-lag accounts only, representing model layer after upstream blocking).
metric: k=1 two-stage ROC-AUC=0.980 [0.976,0.984]; mp_raw PR-AUC=0.892 [0.880,0.903]; fleet_residual mp_raw PR=0.948 / 91.8% prec
result: Two-stage embedding beats trivial at k=1 (ROC=0.980 vs 0.943, Δ+0.037, non-overlapping 95% CIs). PR-AUC is the honest metric at 1:100: mp_raw PR=0.892 vs trivial PR=0.104 (8.6x lift). Rank-norm collapses PR from 0.892 to 0.215. Fleet blocklist model (lag=10d, window=30d): blocklist catches 61% of fleet accounts post-lag (310 TP, two_stage_blocklist PR=0.474); fleet_residual view (pre-lag only) shows mp_raw PR=0.948 / 91.8% prec on cold-start window. combined scorer ROC > mp_raw (0.998 vs 0.992) but PR < mp_raw (0.771 vs 0.918) — ranking artifact from forcing post-lag events to score=1.0.
